subject: Hearthwell benchmarking MAP & proposed test plan
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Park <emily.park@hearthwell.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hearthwell benchmarking MAP & proposed test plan

Thanks again for the time today, Emily — great conversation. Per our call, I'm attaching a first-draft mutual action plan and a concise performance benchmarking outline so your engineering and procurement teams can align on acceptance criteria. High-level goal: validate streaming chat TTFT and steady-state token latency at target concurrency so Hearthwell can go live on the Redwood Dedicated tier.

Proposed acceptance checks we want to cover in the MAP:
- TTFT (time-to-first-token) at target payloads (8k and 2k context) — measure p50/p95/p99
- Per-token streaming latency (single-token emission) under sustained concurrency (2, 8, 16 users simulated)
- Throughput (tokens/sec) and end-to-end RPS at target SLA windows
- Degradation behavior and graceful fallback (model variant/region) during spike tests

Quick test plan (detailed in attached MAP):
1) Baseline single-request profiling (low conc): run 1000 single chats for 2k context to get p50/p95/p99 TTFT.
2) Streamed session ramp: simulate 2, 8, 16 concurrent chat sessions, 30-minute sustained window; record per-token latency distribution and KV-cache hit profile.
3) Spike & recovery: 2x and 4x burst ramps for 5 minutes to validate autoscale/fallback.
4) Regression checks: run the same prompt set used in your quality evals to ensure output parity with our hosted variant.

Deliverables and timeline (proposed):
- Week 0 (this week): sign-off on MAP and test dataset
- Week 1: Redwood runs internal run and shares raw CSV + plots
- Week 2: Joint run with Hearthwell in Dedicated staging; ops fine-tune batching/quantization profile
- Week 3: Final acceptance report and SLO sign-off

Can you confirm the target concurrency you want Redwood to prioritize (I heard 8 during the call) and whether you prefer us to run initial tests with your sample prompts or Redwood's anonymized synthetic workload?

Thanks,
Rafael
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments referenced: hearthwell_map_v2.pdf (MAP & test matrix)

Subject: Re: Hearthwell benchmarking MAP & proposed test plan

Thanks, Rafael — this looks like exactly what we need. Quick answers:
- Confirmed target concurrency: start with 8 concurrent active chat sessions, but we need capacity headroom to tolerate spikes to 32.
- We'll share a redacted set (50 prompts) from our production prompts that exercise typical user flows; please treat as sensitive.
- For acceptance SLOs, our procurement counterpart is asking for p95 TTFT <= 220 ms for 2k context and p95 streaming token latency <= 35 ms at 8 conc. p99 targets are softer but we'd like the numbers.

Can Redwood run the baseline using our prompts first and then your synthetic workload to compare? Also, our security team will need the test logs/audit IDs for the joint run. Liam will coordinate on logistics.

- Emily

Rafa/Monica — quick internal plan so we don't duplicate effort:
- Monica: you'll run Redwood's internal baseline (step 1 + 2) using both synthetic and the 50 redacted Hearthwell prompts (we'll get the file from Emily). Aim to capture: TTFT p50/p95/p99, per-token latency distribution, and KV cache hit rates.
- Connor: please stand by for load harness config to simulate 8/16/32 concurrency. Use continuous streaming mode with 2s inter-token pacing disabled so we measure runtime emission cost.
- Rafael: confirm legal/procurement wants a CSV export + plotted p50/p95/p99 for each conc bucket. Also note: include hardware spec in the report (GPU type, quantization profile, batch size).

Timeline: Monica runs internal baseline Wed-Thu, joint run scheduled next Mon (26th) pending Emily sign-off. If we can finish internal by Thu EOD, we can give Emily raw CSVs ahead of the joint run.

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 22 Mar 2028 14:15:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Hearthwell benchmarking MAP & proposed test plan — internal baseline results

Attaching the raw CSV and three plots (streaming_latency_plots_20280322.png). Summary below (internal baseline on Redwood Dedicated staging cluster: 4x A100 40GB, model variant: rw-large-quant-v2, batcher configured to max_batch_tokens=8192, kv_cache warmed):

Test 1 — Single-request baseline (2k context, Hearthwell prompts, N=1,000):
- TTFT p50 = 95 ms
- TTFT p95 = 208 ms
- TTFT p99 = 345 ms
Notes: p99 skew driven by a small set of prompts with long system prompts and heavy generation (>600 tokens).

Test 2 — Sustained streaming sessions (30 min)
- Concurrency 2 (active sessions):
  - streaming token p50 = 6 ms
  - streaming token p95 = 18 ms
  - streaming token p99 = 43 ms
  - avg tokens/sec/server = 18,200
- Concurrency 8:
  - streaming token p50 = 8 ms
  - streaming token p95 = 28 ms
  - streaming token p99 = 62 ms
  - avg tokens/sec/server = 17,100
- Concurrency 16:
  - streaming token p50 = 12 ms
  - streaming token p95 = 44 ms
  - streaming token p99 = 120 ms
  - avg tokens/sec/server = 15,400

Test 3 — Spike & recovery (5 min 4x traffic):
- Observed autoscale hand-off at ~90s, small sustained increase in p95 TTFT (~+60 ms) during scale; fallback to a compatible model variant avoided outages. Recovery to baseline within 3 minutes.

Observations / recommended config for Hearthwell:
- With rw-large-quant-v2 and current batch settings, we comfortably meet Hearthwell's p95 TTFT target of 220 ms at 8 concurrency (we measured 208 ms). p99 is higher than their preferred soft target — propose a canary with slightly tighter batching (max_batch_tokens=6144) to reduce high-tail p99 for long generations.
- For streaming token latency at 8 conc: p95=28 ms meets the requested <=35 ms. p99=62 ms is elevated; many p99 samples correlate with tokenized prompts producing long first-chunk generation and CPU-side post-processing spikes.
- Suggested joint-run tweaks: enable prefix cache pinning for Hearthwell's common system prompts and run one canary with reduced quantization aggressiveness for high-tail workloads.

Files attached: hearthwell_perf_results_20280322.csv (raw samples) and streaming_latency_plots_20280322.png (p50/p95/p99 curves per-concurrency).

Let me know if you want me to produce a short one-page summary for procurement that highlights the p95/p99 numbers and recommended mitigations.

- Monica
Perf Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 24 Mar 2028 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Hearthwell benchmarking MAP & proposed test plan — results and next steps

Emily — sharing the internal baseline Monica ran (attached). Highlights in plain language:
- We meet your p95 TTFT target (208 ms measured) at 8 concurrent sessions using your prompts.
- Streaming token p95 at 8 conc is 28 ms (within your <=35 ms SLO). p99 is higher (62 ms); Monica included recommended mitigations to reduce the high tail.
- Autoscale behaved as expected during a 4x spike; no service interruption and recovery completed in ~3 minutes.

Proposed MAP updates based on results:
- Week 0 (signed): finalize test dataset and governance (Emily/legal)
- Week 1 (done internally): Redwood baseline run (delivered)
- Week 2 (Mar 26): Joint Dedicated-stage run with Hearthwell engineers; we will apply cache pinning and one reduced-quant canary variant. We'll provide live audit IDs for your security team.
- Week 3 (Apr 2): Final acceptance report and SLO sign-off; procurement to close on Dedicated commit after report acceptance.

Action items for Hearthwell: please upload the 50 redacted prompts to the shared Drive link and confirm that procurement is comfortable with the proposed p99 mitigation (we'll show the canary data during the joint run). Connor will send the load-harness instructions by EOD tomorrow.

If this timeline looks good I'll update the MAP and push v3 to the shared link.

Best,
Rafael
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
